transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 38m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Lumenry Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (Lumenry Platform Eng), Priya Mehta (Lumenry SRE)

Summary: quick results review from last week's soak, retune of batching windows, discuss concurrency caps and queue depth, decide on a 2-hour soak and next steps.

Topics: throughput numbers, continuous batching tweaks, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure, KV cache warmup, fallbacks and burst capacity

[00:00] Samira: All right hey everyone thanks for joining. we'll try to keep it tight—38 minutes on the calendar—this is our weekly standup for the Lumenry pilot. quick round of who is on the call?
[00:10] Aisha: Hi this is Aisha, um head of ML at Lumenry. Daniel and Priya are here too.
[00:15] Daniel: Hey folks.
[00:17] Priya: Hi.
[00:20] Samira: Cool. Ethan from infra side on our end. Ethan, you wanna kick off with the numbers from the test run overnight?
[00:27] Ethan: Yeah quick summary. So we ran the 3-epoch soak for 2 hours with the new continuous batching window at 25ms target, conc limit at 64 per model shard. The headline: steady-state tokens/sec improved about 18% versus last week but P95 latency regressed a bit—went from ~210ms to ~260ms for the long prompt bucket. So better throughput but slightly worse tail.
[00:48] Aisha: Ok, so throughput up is good but that P95 hit is what we saw in prod, right? our success criteria was P95 under 250ms for the single-turn use-case.
[00:58] Samira: Right. The tradeoff is continuous batching aggressively bundles prefixes which helps tokens/s but can add queuing for the long sequence requests—especially when concurrency hits the shard cap. We suspected that.
[01:12] Daniel: We also noticed a couple spikes where request queuing went up to 130 requests in the software queue, even though Redwood's in-flight queue at the serving side stayed under 48. So there's a mismatch between our client-side fanout and the per-shard concurrency.
[01:30] Ethan: Yep and small note—the KV cache warmup is still a factor. Long prompts that have poor cache hit produce more compute and longer tail. We saw KV hit rates jump from 36% to 61% over the run but the earlier minutes are rough.
[01:48] Priya: That's important. Those first 10 minutes skew the P95. Any quick wins to avoid that warmup tail?
[01:54] Ethan: Two immediate ideas: prefix-primer warmup traffic before handing to prod, or a brief model fallback on the first request to a lighter quantized variant until cache warms. Both have tradeoffs.
[02:06] Aisha: We prefer not to return a lower-quality model for any real customer traffic. If fallback is internal test traffic ok but we can't degrade in prod. Primer traffic is doable.
[02:17] Samira: Noted. For the POC we usually recommend a tiny pre-warm step in the client start-up: fire low-cost primer requests with the same prefixes. Been effective on other pilots.
[02:26] Daniel: Alright. On concurrency—we were pushing conc up to 96 last run and hitting queuing. Is 64 the sweet spot?
[02:34] Ethan: From the experiment curve, beyond 64 conc per shard the marginal throughput gains drop and tail jumps non-linearly. So suggestion: cap to 64 with short burst allowance to 80 for short windows, and let continuous batching run at 25ms. We also tightened the batching max batch size to 128 to avoid huge single-batch stalls.
[02:55] Aisha: How about adaptive concurrency—could Redwood auto-throttle?
[02:59] Ethan: Yes we can enable a soft backpressure policy—essentially rate shaping per-client token rate and fall back to smaller model variant under overload. But again, smaller model fallback is a policy decision for Lumenry.
[03:12] Samira: Let's call out policies: 1) recommended: cap conc=64, burst to 80 for 30s windows, batching window 25ms, max batch size 128. 2) pre-warm primer traffic in the first minute after deploy. 3) enable KV cache tracing to monitor warmup.
[03:28] Priya: If we do burst to 80, we need to ensure our autoscaler and network egress isn't overwhelmed—we're on a tight VPC egress quota. I can check limits.
[03:37] Daniel: Also curious about queue depth tuning—we saw the software queue (client side) hitting 130 but the worker queue lower. Should we backpressure at the client earlier?
[03:47] Ethan: Yes move client-side queue cap to 60 and fail-fast or retry with jitter beyond that; it's better than keeping requests queued for long. Redwood has an SDK flag for queueDepth and backoff behavior—we'll include sample config.
[03:59] Samira: Good call. Action item: Ethan will send sample client SDK flags.
[04:07] Ethan: I'll also include the curl/req examples for continuous batching and a small script to simulate primer traffic.
[04:14] Aisha: Perfect.
[04:16] Daniel: Quick question on metrics—can you provide per-model-shard P50/P95 and batch size distribution? The dashboard yesterday had aggregated numbers which hid the hot shard behavior.
[04:27] Ethan: Yes we can split by shard and route. We'll add per-shard panels and export CSV with batch size histogram.
[04:33] Priya: Also please include tokenization breakdown—short vs long tokens; some of our requests are 1k tokens occasionally and those blow up the tail.
[04:41] Samira: We'll annotate the run with request size buckets: <128 tokens, 128-512, 512-1k, >1k.
[04:48] Aisha: On the cost side—how much did continuous batching change estimated spend? We need delta for finance.
[04:54] Ethan: Rough calc: tokens/second up 18% so raw token compute cost up by ~20% but per-user amortized cost falls due to fewer wasted cycles—net pilot cost projection up 8% on our estimate. We'll send a short spreadsheet.
[05:08] Daniel: Hmm finance will want tighter. Any quantization opportunities?
[05:12] Ethan: We have quantized model variants (4-bit) that look close in quality on our evals for your use-case. Switching to quantized for some routes drops cost ~30% and reduces p95 a bit but may impact exactness for the few long-generation prompts.
[05:25] Aisha: We're reluctant to quantize the primary route. Maybe use it for non-customer-facing lengthy async jobs.
[05:32] Samira: Good pragmatic approach—use quantized for batch/async routes, keep full-precision for latency-sensitive real-time routes.
[05:39] Priya: Regarding burst capacity—if we need a short spike beyond reserved quota can Redwood burst across capacity tiers? We have a constrained procurement lead time.
[05:47] Ethan: We have a burst pool option to absorb short spikes, subject to capacity and pricing. For the POC we can provision temporary burst for a test window; Samira will add the burst pricing note.
[05:58] Samira: Yup I'll add that to the pricing sheet.
[06:02] Daniel: Ok next, we saw one error class in logs—503s when batches overflowed the model's queue. Any mitigation?
[06:11] Ethan: Two mitigations: smaller max batch size and fail-fast at client queue cap. Also we can enable request prioritization so short requests get served ahead of long ones. That reduces tail for the small bucket.
[06:23] Aisha: Prioritization sounds useful. How complex is it to configure?
[06:27] Ethan: A flag at routing layer, we can route by approximate request token-length header. We'll provide guidance.
[06:33] Priya: We'll need to add header to the request path then. No problem.
[06:36] Samira: Cool. Let's enumerate the concrete experiment for next soak:
[06:40] Ethan: Experiment plan: 1) client queue cap=60 with fail-fast+retry jitter, 2) conc cap=64, burst to 80 for 30s at most, 3) batching window 25ms, max batch size 128, 4) enable shard-level metrics + batch histogram, 5) pre-warm primer traffic for 60s before traffic ramp, 6) prioritization by token-length header on routing.
[07:07] Daniel: We'll run 2-hour soak at 4k synthetic qps with a mixed request size distribution and share logs.
[07:14] Aisha: If after soak we still miss P95, can we schedule a KV-cache deep-dive?
[07:20] Ethan: Definitely. We can also propose a warm cache proxy pattern if primer doesn't suffice.
[07:25] Samira: Okay timeline and owners—I'll recap after. Any other blockers?
[07:29] Priya: I'll check VPC egress for burst and confirm by Monday.
[07:33] Daniel: I'll kick off the soak after Ethan shares the config.
[07:37] Aisha: Finance will want the cost deltas. Samira you'll send that.
[07:41] Samira: Yup.
[07:43] [crosstalk] Ethan: I'll post the runbook in the shared drive and tag you all.
[07:48] Samira: Great. Recap: next steps = send pricing, batching config, sample SDK flags, run 2-hour soak, check VPC egress, prepare shard-level panels. If soak meets P95<250ms for the 0-512 bucket we move to extended pilot. If not, schedule KV cache deep-dive and consider fallback policies.
[08:12] Daniel: Sounds good.
[08:14] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[08:16] Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up with the deliverables and get the soak scheduled.

Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., CVPC vs VPC), some timestamps approximate.
